correctness.rationale: The marked odd-multiplicity binary-overpartition count satisfies exactly the semi-Pell recurrence by the two disjoint odd-unit cases and even scaling, including base values. Positive-coefficient extraction at u=k/2^k bounds unrestricted binary partitions by the k-dependent product, whose tail is uniformly convergent; the first k-ceil(log2 k) factors give the sharp upper second-order term. For each k>=8, an independent injection of products of integer ranges into overpartitions of 2^k-1 gives the matching lower term, with the leftover unit count provably positive and odd. Strict increase along odd indices transfers the endpoint result uniformly. The Python standard-library verifier compared all coefficients 0..512 by two structurally distinct enumerations and checked dyadic endpoint bounds for k=8..19. The finite checks are not the proof of the asymptotic, which is the symbolic counting argument.

originality.rationale: The same sequence is known, and binary partition asymptotics are classical, but the inspected semi-Pell papers provide recurrences, partition interpretations, congruences and an open growth-comparison motivation without the displayed exact coefficient -1 on the log n log log n term. Unrestricted binary partition asymptotics provide an upper envelope, not the necessary restriction-sensitive lower envelope; the explicit multi-parameter injection supplies it. A previously accessible related odd-partition claim only controls the first term with O(k log k) error, which cannot determine this new second-order coefficient or O(k) remainder. Targeted published-record searches and primary literature and database comparisons yielded no equivalent or dominating published claim. Prior priority and more general asymptotic transfer remain risks, rather than proven absence.
residual_risks: A general theorem for lacunary restricted weighted partitions could imply the result without specifically naming semi-Pell.
The classical Mahler--de Bruijn 1948 original article was not inspected in full; the known unrestricted asymptotic was checked via OEIS and used only as contextual comparison.
Published-record semantic retrieval is not a comprehensive proof of publication priority; no independent expert audit was performed.

value.rationale: A 2023 study explicitly proposes comparing odd-index growth of several self-similar sequences. The new result gives a precise two-term logarithmic asymptotic with O(log n) error for the semi-Pell family and separates the dominant quadratic-logarithmic term from a non-negligible logarithm-times-log-log correction. That correction has the same order as the uncertainty left in the earlier coarse bound and requires a restriction-sensitive injection. The result covers all odd indices rather than a chosen finite range. It does not purport to settle full relative-growth comparisons or lower-order oscillation.
